value: Brain responses to incentive conflict were revealed through comparison of AB and CD; the highest activity attributable to incentive conflict was observed within the striatum (putamen), with prefrontal regions also engaged, notably the ventromedial prefrontal cortex, gyrus rectus, and superior frontal gyrus, as well as the supplementary motor area.
These regions were distinct from those activated in comparator conditions, indicating a distinct motivational meaning of the compound stimulus relative to its individual elements.

value: Gray matter volume was negatively related to number of detoxifications in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex and superior frontal gyrus, with r = −.302 and r = −.192, respectively.

These represent small-to-medium effects, with gray matter volume and number of detoxifications sharing about 9% of variance in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex and 3.7% in the superior frontal gyrus.
